summary: The Vistiq is Cadillac's three-row flagship EV for Australia, sold in a single fully-loaded Platinum grade (now MY27) at $116,000 before on-road costs: sharp enough to undercut a Kia EV9 GT-Line, a Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy and a twin-motor Volvo EX90, though not the single-motor EX90 Plus. Australian reviewers rate the cabin, the AKG audio and the six-seat layout highly, and agree the drivetrain is far quicker than the class needs. Where they diverge is whether the Europe-spec 91kWh pack is enough: 461km of WLTP range and a 130kW DC charging ceiling are both below what the price and the badge imply, and the brand's tiny local footprint makes resale the open question.
pros: At $116,000 before on-roads it undercuts the Kia EV9 GT-Line ($121,000), Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy ($119,668) and twin-motor Volvo EX90 ($134,990) while arriving in top Platinum trim only: 22-inch wheels, adaptive air suspension, rear-wheel steering, four-zone climate, a 33-inch curved display and 23-speaker AKG audio are all standard, with no options ladder to climb
Second-row captain's chairs leave a walk-through aisle to the third row, which CarExpert found fine for a 180cm adult on headroom, though the seat sits knees-up
459kW/880Nm dual-motor AWD covers 0-100km/h in 4.2 seconds, quicker than any EV9 including the GT

5-year/unlimited-km warranty with five years of premium roadside assistance and an 8-year/160,000km battery warranty; MY27 cars stretch service intervals to 24 months/24,000km (complimentary servicing applies only to the MY25 Lyriq, not the Vistiq)
cons: DC charging peaks at just 130kW, the slowest of its direct rivals (EV Central lists the EX90 at 250kW and the EV9 at 210kW), so long trips cost more time than the price suggests
461km WLTP from the 91kWh usable pack (the US car gets 102kWh) trails the Kia EV9 Earth's 512km and the Ioniq 9's 600km, in a 2.9-tonne SUV that is thirsty at a claimed 22kWh/100km

Six seats only in Australia, with no ISOFIX or top tethers in the third row, and only 297L behind the third row to the window line (Cadillac's 430L is the US to-the-roof figure); no front boot and no spare wheel
Resale is the brand risk: Cadillac sells through a handful of Australian stores and the closely related Lyriq took a permanent $32,000 price cut in 2026, which drags residuals across the range
